title: Table reservation lifecycle
idea: The reservation lifecycle is a small state machine: a Reservation starts CONFIRMED, moves to SEATED, CANCELLED or NO_SHOW, and only SEATED moves on to COMPLETED.
points: CONFIRMED moves to SEATED on arrival, CANCELLED by the customer, or NO_SHOW.
SEATED can only become COMPLETED; the other three end states are final.
NO_SHOW is allowed only after the start time plus a grace period.
Active states (CONFIRMED, SEATED) block the table; final states free it.

messages.label: book(4, 19:00)
messages.note: The customer asks for a table for four. Page 3's allocation picks T3.

messages.label: RV-1 CONFIRMED
messages.note: The reservation starts CONFIRMED. It now blocks T3 from 19:00 to 20:30.

messages.label: seat(RV-1)
messages.note: Happy path: the party arrives and the host seats them. CONFIRMED moves to SEATED.

messages.label: finish(RV-1)
messages.note: The party leaves. SEATED moves to COMPLETED, a final state.

messages.label: sweep(19:10)
messages.note: Other path: the sweeper runs at 19:10. Grace is 15 minutes, so nothing changes yet.

messages.label: sweep(19:16)
messages.note: At 19:16 the sweeper moves RV-2, another 19:00 booking whose party is absent, to NO_SHOW. Its table frees.

messages.label: seat(RV-2)
messages.note: That party walks in at 19:20. NO_SHOW is final, so the service refuses.

messages.label: refused: final
messages.note: The host seats them as a walk-in instead, if a table is free.

code.title: Status enum with rules
code.caption: The allowed moves live in the enum. Times are passed in, so the no-show rule replays the same way.

walk.text: RV-1 takes the happy path: seated, then completed.
RV-2: a no-show check too early, one after grace, then a late arrival.
RV-3 is cancelled, then cancelled again by a double click.
An `EnumMap` lists allowed next states; missing states get an empty set.
`canMoveTo` is the one question; `isFinal` means no arrows leave.
A time guard sits on top of the state rule for no-shows.
Refuse and report an illegal move; otherwise record the new state.

pitfalls: Do not set `status` from controllers; every change goes through one `moveTo`.
Mark no-shows only after the grace period, using the injected time, never the wall clock.
Treat a second cancel as a refused move, not a crash or a silent success.

quiz.q: What does ReservationLifecycle print when RV-2 is seated late?
options: RV-2 too early for no-show at 19:20
quiz.why: The 19:16 sweep moved RV-2 to NO_SHOW. NO_SHOW has no allowed next states, so `moveTo` refuses and tags it final.

takeaway: Write allowed transitions once, in the enum, and refuse everything else.

starters: Should a late party be able to undo a no-show?
How does the sweeper find reservations to mark?
Would a PENDING state help if deposits were added?
